title: Four Indian Medical Students Injured in Neo-Nazi Knife Attack at Russian University
excerpt: A 15-year-old linked to a banned extremist group stabbed four Indian students at Bashkir State Medical University in Ufa, prompting India's embassy to dispatch officials and AIMSA to appeal to PM Modi for stronger safety measures abroad.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • A 15-year-old attacker injured seven, including four Indian students, at Bashkir State Medical University in Russia.
  • The attacker is linked to the banned neo-Nazi group National Socialism/White Power, designated a terrorist organization.
  • India's embassy sent officials to assist victims; AIMSA urged PM Modi for enhanced safety measures for students abroad.
  • Russian authorities opened criminal cases for attempted murder and negligence regarding the attacker's known behavioral issues.

  • A 15-year-old armed with a knife, pepper spray, and firecrackers attacked students at a Bashkir State Medical University dormitory in Ufa, Russia on February 7, injuring seven people including four Indian medical students.
  • Russian investigators linked the attacker to the banned neo-Nazi group National Socialism/White Power (NS/WP), designated a terrorist organisation by Russia's Supreme Court in 2021.
  • India's embassy in Moscow dispatched consular officials from Kazan; the All India Medical Students' Association (AIMSA) wrote to PM Modi demanding stronger safety protocols for Indian students abroad.
  • Russian authorities opened criminal cases for attempted murder and negligence, citing officials' failure to act on known behavioural warning signs about the suspect.

A 15-year-old armed with a knife attacked students at a dormitory of the Bashkir State Medical University in Ufa, Bashkortostan, on February 7, injuring seven people — including four Indian medical students and two police officers — in what investigators believe was a hate-motivated assault linked to a banned neo-Nazi organisation, according to Reuters and Russian law enforcement.

The attacker entered the foreign students' hostel carrying a knife, pepper spray, firecrackers, and brass knuckles. He set off firecrackers, then slashed at students and a security guard who tried to intervene. Some students barricaded themselves in their rooms as the attack unfolded. Videos circulated on Russian media showed blood on dormitory floors and broken door windows.

Victims and Response

Of the four Indian students hospitalised, one was in serious condition with stab wounds to the abdomen and back, while three others were in moderate condition with injuries including cuts to the face, arms, and neck, according to Interfax. A security guard was stabbed in the thigh and jaw while attempting to stop the attacker. Two police officers were also injured when the suspect resisted arrest.

"The attacker resisted arrest, during which two police officers were stabbed. Furthermore, the suspect also inflicted bodily harm on himself," Russia's Interior Ministry spokesperson Maj. General Irina Volk said, as quoted by RTVI.

One victim was discharged later the same day. The attacker was admitted to a children's hospital in serious condition with self-inflicted injuries.

Neo-Nazi Links

Russian investigative outlet Baza reported that the suspect was a supporter of the National Socialism/White Power (NS/WP) organisation, which was designated a terrorist group by Russia's Supreme Court in 2021. During the attack, he reportedly shouted nationalist slogans referencing the Holocaust and drew a swastika on a wall using a victim's blood.

The suspect, identified only as Alexander S., was described by acquaintances as a quiet student who lived with his 51-year-old disabled mother and 67-year-old grandmother. He had no father, and the family was very poor, according to Russian media reports. No security guards were on duty at the dormitory at the time — they were only scheduled from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. under a 9-million-rouble security contract signed in late 2025.

Diplomatic and Institutional Fallout

The Indian Embassy in Moscow described the stabbing as "an unfortunate incident" and confirmed it was in contact with Russian authorities. Officials from India's Consulate in Kazan were dispatched to Ufa to assist the injured students.

The All India Medical Students' Association (AIMSA) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, calling the attack "unacceptable" and urging the government to take diplomatic steps to ensure justice, strengthen safety mechanisms for Indian students abroad, issue emergency advisories, and coordinate with foreign universities to prevent future incidents.

"Indian students travel overseas with dreams of becoming healthcare professionals and serving humanity. Any act of violence, discrimination, or hostility against them is unacceptable and must be strongly condemned."

— All India Medical Students' Association, in letter to PM Modi

Criminal Investigation

Russia's Investigative Committee opened criminal cases under two articles: attempted murder of two or more persons, and encroachment on the life of a law enforcement officer. A second case was filed for negligence, citing school officials and youth protection authorities who were aware of behavioural warning signs but failed to take preventive action, according to Reuters.

What It Means for Indian Students in Russia

Russia hosts one of the largest populations of Indian medical students abroad, with tens of thousands enrolled across universities in cities from Moscow to Kazan to Ufa. The attack has intensified concerns about campus security at Russian institutions, particularly for foreign students. AIMSA's appeal underscored a broader demand for systemic changes — including emergency helplines and stricter monitoring of safety conditions at universities where Indian students are enrolled.
